content.text:
That's the page I worked from when I first set up BYOK, and it backs up what the test compiles showed. No changes needed.

- **Base URL:** it says "Set `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` in `engine.env` to activate BYOK mode." That's why the variable stays even though `providers.json` has the same URL.
- **Allowlist:** a literal base URL gets its host added to the firewall allowlist automatically, for both the agent and the threat-detection run. That's why only Aperture's host has to be listed by hand.
- **Credentials:** the real key stays in gh-aw's API proxy, and the agent only sees a dummy one. That's moot here since your gateways don't check keys.

One item on that page to remember: it recommends `engine.model-catalog: false` for BYOK providers that don't serve a `/models` list. Without it, gh-aw checks the model name against that list before the run and stops if it can't fetch one. Your local gh-aw (v1.2.2) rejects that field, so I left it out. If the first run stops with `catalog_unavailable`, update gh-aw and add the field.

Ready for the next item on your list.

content:
<pasted_content id="c9d5">
Model aliases
Note
Copilot catalogs vary by organization and can lag seat offerings, so another workflow’s model inventory does not prove availability here. An exact Copilot ID missing from a complete live catalog is not offered to this workflow; prefer `opus` or `sonnet`. Run `gh aw audit <run-url> --models` for run-specific catalog and routing details. Incomplete discovery does not confirm absence.
Copilot, Claude, Codex, Pi, and Agy resolve aliases against the configured provider’s live AWF `/reflect` catalog before execution:

* Built-in aliases (such as `opus`/`small`), workflow-defined `models:`, and their globs select the newest live match. Globs skip models AWF marks as not automatically selectable, such as a Decisions-only evaluation model; alias entries without `*`, such as `evals`, are unaffected.
* A `provider/` prefix restricts the lookup; otherwise the engine’s configured provider applies.
* Exact live IDs take precedence over same-named aliases, and unrecognized IDs are not rewritten. Pi checks exact IDs before launch; Copilot, Claude, and Codex fail on the first unavailable-model request.
* `auto` keeps its engine-specific meaning. In Copilot CLI mode, `?effort=low`, `?effort=medium`, and `?effort=high` on a model ID or alias become `--reasoning-effort` after alias resolution. The CLI receives the model ID without the suffix. An explicit `--reasoning-effort` in `engine.args` takes precedence.
* Missing matches fail with `model_unavailable`; incomplete discovery fails with `catalog_unavailable`.

Set `engine.model-catalog: false` (default `true`) for BYOK providers without a `/models` route, such as Azure AI Gateway. The configured model is then passed to the engine verbatim: aliases are not resolved, and a model ID that matches a built-in alias (such as `gpt-5-mini`) no longer fails with `catalog_unavailable`. Model routing also needs the catalogue, so the implicit routing default is not applied and `model: router` fails compilation. Threat detection inherits the workflow `model`; when none is set, it uses the engine’s main-agent default instead of the `detection` alias.
`engine.copilot-sdk: true` also needs the catalogue, so combining it with `model-catalog: false` fails compilation; use Copilot CLI mode instead.
Sub-agent models are also passed verbatim, without catalogue or endpoint checks; a Claude or Codex sub-agent model whose `provider/` prefix names a different provider still fails.
Workflow-defined `models:` aliases are not resolved either: naming one passes the alias name to the engine as a literal model ID and logs a warning, so set a concrete model ID instead.

```
engine:
```

`id: copilot`
`model: gpt-5-mini`
`model-catalog: false`
Gemini and declarative engines pass model names through unchanged and warn about gh-aw aliases. AWF can independently rewrite unrecognized models on non-Copilot providers; disable `sandbox.agent.model-fallback` when exact routing is required.
Resolution produces `model.resolution` evidence in `usage/aw_session.jsonl`. See [Model Aliases](https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/model-tables/) for the catalog and [Model Routing](https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/model-routing/) for experimental per-run model/effort selection on Copilot-backed Copilot, Claude, Codex, and Pi, chosen with `model: router` (or `router/economy`, `router/balanced`, `router/robust`). Router values are not model names: `router` and `router/*` are reserved and can’t be used as aliases.
</pasted_content id="c9d5">

content.text:
That section matters here in two places. I'd still not change anything until the first run.

**1. `model-catalog: false` isn't available to you yet.** v1.2.2 is the latest gh-aw release (Nov 10), and it rejects the field. It's documented, but only exists on gh-aw's main branch. So the default applies: before the agent starts, gh-aw checks the model name against the model list it gets from the gateway.
- **Does `anthropic-oauth-proxy` have a model list?** It has no `/models` route of its own. Its catch-all route (`main.rs:62`, `.fallback(proxy_handler)`) should forward `GET /v1/models` to Anthropic. I haven't confirmed that Anthropic answers that call for OAuth-authenticated requests.
- **If the list can't be fetched,** the run stops with `catalog_unavailable` before the agent does anything. That's when updating gh-aw and adding `model-catalog: false` becomes necessary.

**2. The `lab-proxy/` prefix is the bigger unknown.** The docs say "a `provider/` prefix restricts the lookup". To the Copilot CLI, `lab-proxy/claude-opus-5-5` means "this model from that entry in providers.json". gh-aw may instead read `lab-proxy` as one of its own providers, which it doesn't know.
- **Best case:** it's treated as unrecognized and passed through ("unrecognized IDs are not rewritten"), and the CLI resolves it.
- **Worst case:** the lookup fails with `model_unavailable` or `catalog_unavailable`.

If the first run fails on this, there's a fix that works on v1.2.2 without `model-catalog`:
- Rename Aperture's model entry to a unique ID, such as `claude-opus-5-5-aperture`, with `"wireModel": "claude-opus-5-5"` so Aperture still receives the real name.
- Set `model: claude-opus-5-5` with no prefix. That's a real Anthropic model ID that matches only `lab-proxy`.

I haven't confirmed the CLI resolves an unprefixed ID to a `providers.json` model either; its docs only show the `PROVIDER/MODEL` form.

**Already fine:**
- Threat detection inherits the workflow's `model`, and that job checks out the repo, so it gets the same `providers.json`.
- We don't use `models:` aliases or `copilot-sdk`, so those restrictions don't apply.

When it runs, `gh aw audit <run-url> --models` will show how the model was resolved.

content.text:
I upgraded gh-aw to v1.4.1 and added `model-catalog: false`. Evals still can't use your gateways, even with the `model` override from the section you found. Nothing is committed.

**Upgrade**
- **Version:** v1.2.2 is still gh-aw's latest stable release. `model-catalog` arrived in v1.4.0 ("Add engine.model-catalog to skip live model-catalogue resolution for BYOK providers"). I installed v1.4.1, which is marked as a prerelease. I first checked that the matching `github/gh-aw-actions/setup@v1.4.1` tag exists, since the compiled workflow downloads it.
- **Pinned:** the extension is pinned to that version, so `gh extension upgrade` won't move it. To upgrade again, run `gh extension install github/gh-aw --pin <version>`.
- **Workflow:** `engine.model-catalog: false`, with a comment explaining it. The compiled lock now has `MODEL_CATALOG: false`, still no `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` check, and `COPILOT_MODEL: lab-proxy/claude-opus-5-5`. This also handles the `lab-proxy/` prefix worry from before: with the catalog off, gh-aw passes the model name through without looking it up.
- **Docker warning:** v1.4.1 warned that the prompt asks the agent to use Docker. That was the `docker build .` command in the reproduction table, which is advice for you, not the agent. I reworded it, and the strict compile now has 0 warnings.
- **Diff from the upgrade:** the lock and `.github/aw/actions-lock.json` changed (about 350 lines in the lock).

**Evals**
The extended form only lets you choose between gh-aw's two judge providers, Copilot and OpenAI. To check whether the endpoint can be redirected, I compiled a throwaway copy with `model: openai/claude-opus-5-5` and then restored the file. The judge step came out as:
```
GH_AW_DECISIONS_BASE_URL: https://api.openai.com/v1
GH_AW_DECISIONS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CODEX_API_KEY || secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
```
The default is `https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1` with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`. The base URL is written into the step itself, and nothing in the frontmatter can change it. So the judge can't reach either of your gateways. It also needs a `/v1/decisions` endpoint, which neither gateway serves, and the evals job never joins the tailnet.

That leaves three options:
- **Keep the block.** The judge step fails on every run, but it's set to continue on error, so the workflow still finishes and records no scores. The eval questions stay in place for when this becomes possible.
- **Remove `evals:`.** Cleaner runs, but it drops the grader you asked for originally.
- **Add an OpenAI key (`OPENAI_API_KEY`) or a `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, only for the judge.** That's the only way the evals actually run, at the cost of a second inference provider.

What should happen to the evals block: keep it for now, or remove it?

content.text:
Use `gh secret set`. It prompts for the value, so the key doesn't end up in your shell history:

```bash
gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY --repo basher83/tailnet-microservices
```

To pipe it in from a password manager instead, use `--body -`, which reads the value from standard input:

```bash
op read "op://<vault>/<item>/credential" | gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY --repo basher83/tailnet-microservices --body -
```

Then check it's there (this lists names only, never values):

```bash
gh secret list --repo basher83/tailnet-microservices
```

The workflow also needs one change to use the key. The judge still defaults to the Copilot provider, so `evals:` has to switch to the extended form with an OpenAI model. My test compile confirmed this makes the judge use `api.openai.com` with `OPENAI_API_KEY`:

```yaml
evals:
  questions:
    # ...the five existing questions, unchanged
  model: openai/gpt-6-luna
```

`openai/gpt-6-luna` is the OpenAI model gh-aw's evals docs name for `/v1/decisions`. Your key's account needs access to it. Want me to make that change, uncommitted like the rest?

Evals now run on `openai/gpt-6-luna` using your `OPENAI_API_KEY` secret. The workflow compiles with `--strict` and no warnings. Nothing is committed, and no eval has run yet.

**What changed**
- **`evals:` now uses the extended form:** the same five questions, unchanged, under `questions:`, plus `model: openai/gpt-6-luna`. A short comment explains why the judge can't use your gateways.
- **The compiled judge step now has:**
  ```
  GH_AW_DECISIONS_PROVIDER: openai
  GH_AW_DECISIONS_BASE_URL: https://api.openai.com/v1
  GH_AW_DECISIONS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CODEX_API_KEY || secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
  GH_AW_EVALS_MODEL: "openai/gpt-6-luna"
  ```

**Secrets review**
gh-aw's safety gate flagged `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `CODEX_API_KEY` as new secrets. In the compiled file, both appear exactly once, in the evals job's judge step. The agent job, the threat-detection job and the issue-creating job never get them. `CODEX_API_KEY` is only there because gh-aw tries it first and falls back to `OPENAI_API_KEY`. You don't have a `CODEX_API_KEY`, so your OpenAI key is the one used. With that checked, I approved the change.

**Still unconfirmed:** whether your OpenAI account can use `gpt-6-luna` through `/v1/decisions`. If it can't, gh-aw records the evals as not run (`model_unavailable` or `judge_failed`). That step is set to continue on error, so the triage run itself still finishes either way.

Run one or more agentic workflows in trial mode against a simulated repository.

This command creates a temporary private repository in your GitHub account, installs the specified
workflows from their source repositories, and runs them in "trial mode" to capture safe outputs without
making actual changes to the simulated host repository.

Repository modes:
- Default mode (no flags): Creates a temporary trial repository and simulates execution as if running against the current repository (github.repository context points to the current repository)
- --logical-repo REPO: Simulates execution against a specified repository (github.repository context points to REPO while actually running in a temporary trial repository)
- --host-repo REPO: Uses the specified repository as the host for trial execution instead of creating a temporary one
- --clone-repo REPO: Clones the specified repository's contents into the trial repository before execution (useful for testing against actual repository state)

All workflows must support the workflow_dispatch trigger to be used in trial mode.
The host repository will be created as a private repository and retained by default unless --delete-host-repo-after is specified.
Trial results are saved both locally (in the trials/ directory) and in the host repository for future reference.

Usage:
  gh aw trial <workflow-spec>... [flags]

Examples:
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/weekly-research                         # Run a single workflow in a temporary trial repository
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/daily-plan githubnext/agentics/weekly-research # Compare multiple workflows
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/daily-plan myorg/myrepo/custom-workflow # Run workflows from different repositories
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/my-workflow --host-repo myorg/myrepo    # Use an existing host repository
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/my-workflow --logical-repo myorg/myrepo # Simulate a different github.repository value
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/my-workflow --clone-repo myorg/myrepo   # Clone repository contents into the trial host
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/my-workflow --repeat 3                  # Run 4 times total (1 initial + 3 repeats)
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/my-workflow --delete-host-repo-after    # Delete the trial host repository when done
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/my-workflow --dry-run                   # Preview changes without executing
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/my-workflow --json                      # Output trial results in JSON format
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/my-workflow --auto-merge-prs            # Auto-merge PRs created during the trial
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/my-workflow --host-repo .               # Use the current repository as the host
  gh aw trial ./local-workflow.md --clone-repo upstream/repo --repeat 2   # Run a local workflow against cloned contents
  gh aw trial githubnext/agentics/my-workflow --trigger-context https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123 # Provide issue context for issue-triggered workflows

Flags:
      --append string                          Append extra content to the end of the agentic workflow on installation

      --clone-repo string                      Clone the contents of the specified repository into the host repository before execution (useful for testing against actual repository state)
      --delete-host-repo-after[=true|false]    Delete the host repository after completion (retained by default)

content.text:
It's running: [ci-failure-triage run 46141709503](https://github.com/basher83/tailnet-microservices/actions/runs/46141709503), started by a push to the PR branch. I'm watching it in the background and will go through each job when it finishes.

**What I pushed** (commit `73e305b`, PR #60):
- **BYOK setup:** `providers.json` with both gateways, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, and `model-catalog: false`. The lock was recompiled with gh-aw v1.4.1.
- **Tailnet:** a Tailscale step in the agent and threat-detection jobs.
- **Evals:** the judge on `openai/gpt-6-luna` with your `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Your curl shows the key can call `/v1/decisions` with that model.
- **A temporary `pull_request` trigger**, limited to this workflow's own three files. GitHub only allows dispatching workflows whose file is already on `main`, and this one isn't, so this is how it runs before merge. I'll remove the trigger once we've seen a run. Until then, any push that touches those files starts another run.

**What could go wrong, in run order:**
1. **Tailscale login.** OpenWiki only runs on a schedule from `main`. If your tailnet's trust settings for the GitHub login are tied to `main` or to scheduled runs, a run from a PR fails at the "Connect to tailnet" step.
2. **Reaching the gateway from inside the sandbox.** This is the point I couldn't check earlier: whether the agent's containers can look up `*.ts.net` names and connect through the firewall proxy.
3. **Whether `providers.json` and the `lab-proxy/claude-opus-5-5` model name work inside gh-aw's sandbox.**
4. **The evals job.**

This run can file real issues. `CI` on `main` is still red in the Audit job, so expect up to five `[ci-triage]` issues if the agent gets that far.

##### Run from a feature branch

`gh aw run workflow --ref feature/my-change` executes the compiled `.github/workflows/workflow.lock.yml` **from the selected branch**, not the default branch's version. The branch or tag must already be pushed and its lock file must declare `workflow_dispatch`. Without `--ref`, local runs use the current branch; `--repo owner/repo` runs use that repository's default branch.

GitHub [requires the workflow file to exist on the default branch](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/manually-run-a-workflow) before manual dispatch. `--ref` selects workflow content, not registration. Neither `run` nor `trial --host-repo` provides ephemeral registration, changes the default branch, or bypasses this platform requirement.

For an already registered workflow, compile and push the candidate source, lock file, and dependencies to the feature branch, then select that ref:

```bash
gh aw compile workflow --validate --strict
gh aw run workflow --dry-run --ref feature/my-change  # Preview the dispatch
gh aw run workflow --ref feature/my-change

content.content:
## Summary

Adds a [gh-aw](https://github.com/github/gh-aw) agentic workflow, `ci-failure-triage`, that investigates failed GitHub Actions runs once a week and files one root-cause issue per distinct failure.

- **Source:** `.github/workflows/ci-failure-triage.md`
- **Compiled:** `.github/workflows/ci-failure-triage.lock.yml` (`gh aw compile ci-failure-triage --strict`, gh-aw v1.2.2, 0 warnings)
- **Compiler side files:** `.gitattributes` (marks `*.lock.yml` as generated) and `.github/aw/actions-lock.json`

**Intent:** reduce the time spent diagnosing CI failures.

| Engine | `copilot` |
| Agent permissions | Read-only: `actions`, `contents`, `issues`, `pull-requests` |
| Output | `create-issue` only: `max: 5`, prefix `[ci-triage] `, labels `bug` and `github-actions` |
| Memory | `cache-memory` at `ci-failure-triage/state.json` |
- **No `workflow_run` trigger or `if:` on its conclusion.** The requested trigger is a schedule, so that guidance became an explicit list of failing conclusions in the pre-step and the prompt.

## Before this can run

- [ ] **Add the `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` repository secret.** It isn't configured yet. Because this is a personal repo, the `copilot-requests: write` org-billing path isn't available.
- **Cache eviction (addressed).** [GitHub removes caches](https://github.com/github/docs/blob/main/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching.md#usage-limits-and-eviction-policy) that have not been accessed in over 7 days. With a Friday-only schedule, the gap between saving the cache and the next restore was just under 7 days. One failed run would have pushed it to 14, because the cache is only saved after the agent job and the safety check both succeed. With the Tuesday run, runs are at most 4 days apart. A restore probably counts as an access even when that run later fails, but I haven't confirmed that.

## Validation

- `gh aw compile ci-failure-triage --strict` succeeded with 0 warnings.
- The pre-step's `gh run list` and `jq` pipeline was run locally against live data: 11 runs in the window, 9 failures.
- The workflow itself has **not** been run. Today, `CI` on `main` is red in the `Audit` job, along with the Renovate PRs, so the first dispatch should produce a real incident to judge it by.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

content.text:
I merged PR #60 and started the first real run from `main`: [run 46142203840](https://github.com/basher83/tailnet-microservices/actions/runs/46142203840). I'm watching it in the background and will go through each job when it finishes.

**What happened with the first attempt**
- **Why it failed:** the temporary-trigger run never reached the agent. For runs started by a PR, gh-aw reads the prompt from `main` so a PR can't rewrite an agent's instructions. This workflow wasn't on `main` yet, so the prompt file wasn't found.
- **Cleanup:** I removed the temporary trigger in commit `3d4b665` before merging. My first attempt at that edit deleted 356 lines of the workflow source. I caught it before committing, restored the file, and the commit removes only the 8-line block.

**The merge**
- **What I did:** marked the PR ready and merged it with a merge commit (`1219eb6`), matching the repo's history. `main` has no branch protection, and the branch was deleted automatically.
- **PR description:** updated first to describe the BYOK setup, the tailnet steps, the OpenAI evals judge, and the review of the new secrets and action. It no longer says a `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` is needed.
- **Now live:** the Tuesday and Friday schedules, so the next scheduled run is Tuesday around 09:39 UTC. The merge also started `CI` on `main`. Its Audit job is already failing, so that run won't deploy.

The open questions are still the ones from before: the Tailscale login, whether the sandbox can reach the `*.ts.net` gateways, how the CLI handles `providers.json`, and then the issues filed and the evals judge.

#

# never reads providers.json; this variable is how the compiler knows the run is
# BYOK. Without it, the compiled workflow adds a required COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN
# check, drops the gateway from the firewall allowlist, and sets no API-proxy
# target. COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE is not needed: providers.json sets the type.
"""
new_c="""# BYOK: inference goes to gateways on the tailnet, not GitHub Copilot.
# .github/aw/providers.json is what the Copilot CLI uses: both providers, the
# model capabilities, and the wire type. Models are selected as
# <provider>/<model-id>:
#   lab-proxy          -> AWF API-proxy sidecar -> anthropic-oauth-proxy, in use
#   aperture-anthropic -> Aperture on agents.tailfb3ea.ts.net; switch `model:`
#                         to aperture-anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 to use it
#
# Request path for lab-proxy: the agent never dials the gateway itself. AWF
# keeps the real upstream in its API-proxy sidecar, and inside the sandbox the
# Copilot listener is http://172.30.0.30:10002 (what AWF sets
# COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL to there). providers.json overrides that variable,
# so lab-proxy's baseUrl must be the sidecar address itself; pointing it at the
# gateway's https URL bypasses the sidecar and fails with a TLS "wrong version
# number" error (run 46142203840).
#
# COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL (outside the sandbox) is the sidecar's upstream: the
# real gateway. It also makes gh-aw compile the run as BYOK (no
# COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN check) and allowlists the gateway host.
# COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY is a placeholder: the sidecar refuses keyless
# upstreams (503), and the gateway strips client auth headers in OAuth mode, so
# the value never matters. Avoid a bare "-": gh-aw emits it unquoted and the
# generated YAML breaks. COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE is not needed: providers.json
# sets the type.
"""
assert old_c in t; t=t.replace(old_c,new_c)
old_e="""    COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL: https://anthropic-oauth-proxy.tailfb3ea.ts.net
"""
new_e="""    COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL: https://anthropic-oauth-proxy.tailfb3ea.ts.net
    COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY: unused-gateway-strips-auth
"""
assert t.count(old_e)==1; t=t.replace(old_e,new_e); open(p,"w").write(t)
EOF

content.text:
You're right, it was hitting the wrong endpoint. The fix is pushed to a new branch, and a test run from that branch has started: [run 46142756888](https://github.com/basher83/tailnet-microservices/actions/runs/46142756888). `main` is unchanged, and I'm watching the run in the background.

**What was wrong**
- **The sandbox design:** gh-aw's sandbox keeps the real provider URL in a separate proxy container, called the sidecar. Inside the sandbox, AWF points `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` at that sidecar instead of the gateway. The failed run's log shows this:
  ```
  [health-check] COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=http://172.30.0.30:10002 (offline+BYOK mode)
  [health-check] ✓ GitHub Copilot API proxy is reachable at http://172.30.0.30:10002
  ```
- **The conflict:** our `providers.json` gave `lab-proxy` the gateway's `https://anthropic-oauth-proxy…` address, and the CLI uses that file ahead of the variable. So it dialed the gateway directly. Something inside the sandbox answered with plain HTTP, which produced the TLS "wrong version number" error.
- **Not the cause:** your gateway is fine. `k8s/ingress.yaml` serves TLS, and Tailscale connected in this run.

**The fix** (commit `ebcb2d8` on `claude/ci-triage-sidecar-endpoint`)
- **`providers.json`:** `lab-proxy`'s `baseUrl` is now `http://172.30.0.30:10002`. It keeps the model capabilities, and the sidecar still forwards to the real gateway.
- **`COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY: unused-gateway-strips-auth`** in the workflow. The sidecar refuses to forward to an upstream that has no key (it returns 503, per AWF's source). The value is never used: the sidecar swaps in its own key, and your gateway strips client auth headers in OAuth mode.
- **The workflow comment** now explains the request path, so nobody points `baseUrl` back at the gateway.

**Caveats**
- **AWF coupling:** `172.30.0.30:10002` is AWF's documented internal address for the sidecar. If a future AWF release moves it, `providers.json` would have to follow.
- **Aperture** still has its direct `http://agents…` address. The sidecar only forwards to one upstream, so Aperture can't go through it. I haven't tested whether the direct path works.
- **Failure issues:** gh-aw opened [#61](https://github.com/basher83/tailnet-microservices/issues/61) and [#62](https://github.com/basher83/tailnet-microservices/issues/62) automatically for the two failed runs. You can close them once a run succeeds.

**Next to check:** whether the sidecar itself can resolve and reach the `*.ts.net` gateway. That's the next hop in this run.

content.text:
Yes, that's most likely why. AWF's whole BYOK design rests on one rule: the agent never holds the real endpoint or key. The real values live in the sidecar, and the agent only sees environment variables pointing at it. `providers.json` is a file the CLI trusts more than those variables, so it walks straight around that rule. The docs describe only the variable route because that's the only route AWF controls.

Our workaround works because we point `providers.json` back at the sidecar. That ties us to an AWF internal (`172.30.0.30:10002`) that's documented but not promised to stay put.

If this run succeeds, there's a cleaner end state worth weighing: drop `providers.json` and use only the supported variables. `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE: anthropic`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS` and `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` cover the type and token limits. The trade-off is the three capability settings you asked for (vision, adaptive thinking, reasoning effort), which have no variables. The CLI would fall back to its built-in defaults for `claude-opus-5-5`, which probably match, but I haven't verified that. Aperture as a second option would also go away, since the sidecar only forwards to one upstream.

The run is still going, and I'll report back when it finishes.

No, I hadn't checked. I went by gh-aw's table of `COPILOT_PROVIDER_*` variables, which only covers the ones gh-aw handles. The Copilot CLI's own help has the full list, and you're right about vision. I checked your local CLI with `copilot help environment` (version 1.0.118):

| Capability you asked for | Variable | What the help says |
|---|---|---|
| Vision | **`COPILOT_PROVIDER_VISION=true`** | "BYOK models are treated as text-only unless this is set" |
| Token limits | `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | Override the catalog and default values |
| Model behavior defaults | `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID` | "well-known model ID used for agent configuration and token limits" |
| Adaptive thinking (`"required"`) | none found | No variable in that version's list |
| Supported reasoning-effort levels | none found | Only the per-run `--reasoning-effort <level>` flag |

So an env-only setup covers vision and the token limits exactly. Adaptive thinking and the effort list would come from the CLI's built-in defaults for `claude-opus-5-5`, selected through `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID`. A specific effort level can still be set per run, either by adding `?effort=high` to the model name (gh-aw turns it into `--reasoning-effort`) or with that flag directly.

The CI runner installs whatever CLI version gh-aw pins, which may differ from your 1.0.118. If you've seen variables for adaptive thinking or reasoning effort somewhere, point me at it and I'll use them.

content.content:
Environment Variables:

  `COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL`: allow all tools to run automatically without confirmation. Accepts "true", "1", "yes", "on", or "y", case-insensitively and ignoring surrounding whitespace; "false", "0", "no", "off", "n", or an empty value turn it off. Setting it to exactly "true" additionally trusts the working directory without prompting, which loads that directory's skills, plugins, MCP servers, and hooks, including hooks that run shell commands; the other truthy spellings only auto-approve tools.

  `COPILOT_ASSISTED_APPROVAL`: set to "true" (or "1", "yes", "on") to review tool permission requests with the assisted-approval safety judge, like --assisted-approval. Supported only in non-interactive prompt mode (-p); an interactive session refuses to start while it is set.

  `COPILOT_AUTO_TIER`: optionally set the Auto routing profile to "efficiency", "balance", or "intelligence", or a server-advertised profile in local sessions. "fast" is ignored with a notice, because the CLI cannot run on that profile. Requires the effective model to be Auto and is overridden by --auto-tier or persisted configuration.

  `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE`: set to "false" to disable downloading updated CLI versions and the plugin updates run when a session starts. The --no-auto-update flag disables the CLI download only. Auto-update is enabled by default, except in CI environments (detected via `CI`, `BUILD_NUMBER`, `RUN_ID`, or `SYSTEM_COLLECTIONURI` environment variables), where it is disabled by default. Standalone development builds run their bundled package by default and do not offer or install CLI updates unless release-style package behavior is selected with a canonical semantic version in `COPILOT_CLI_VERSION`. `COPILOT_CLI_DIST_DIR` selects an explicit package but does not enable updates for a development-identity package. On other standalone-binary installations, disabling it this way or with --no-auto-update also makes launches ignore any newer version already in the package cache and run the version built into the installed binary.

  `COPILOT_BACKGROUND_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD`: fraction of the model's context window (for example "0.7") at which the CLI starts compacting the conversation in the background; defaults to 0.8 (a few models have their own default).

  `COPILOT_BASH_PATH`: path of the bash executable used for the agent's shell commands and for command hooks. By default the first executable of /bin/bash, /usr/bin/bash, /usr/local/bin/bash, and /run/current-system/sw/bin/bash is used, then bash from PATH; on Windows, bash from PATH.

  `COPILOT_BUFFER_EXHAUSTION_THRESHOLD`: fraction of the model's context window at which compaction blocks the conversation until it finishes; defaults to 0.95.

  `COPILOT_CACHE_HOME`: directory for cached data that can be deleted and re-created, such as downloaded CLI versions. Not affected by COPILOT_HOME. Defaults to `~/Library/Caches/copilot` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\copilot` on Windows, and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/copilot` or `~/.cache/copilot` elsewhere.

  `COPILOT_CHILD_OOM_SCORE_ADJ`: Linux only. The `oom_score_adj` given to shell processes the CLI starts, so that under memory pressure the kernel ends those before the CLI. An integer from -1000 to 1000, or "off" to leave it unchanged; defaults to 300. A child never gets a lower score than the CLI itself.

  `COPILOT_CLI_POLICY_HELPER_FAILURE_MODE`: choose "ignore" (default) to continue with other policy channels when a registered Policy Helper fails, or "failClosed" to engage fail-closed protection. Device-managed settings take precedence over server-managed settings, and both take precedence over this variable. Unrelated managed settings do not suppress this fallback. Invalid values log a warning and use the default.

  `COPILOT_CLI_VERSION`: override the CLI version used for update comparisons. On standalone development builds, a canonical semantic version also opts into release-style cached-package selection and CLI updates, but does not pin cache selection to that exact version or change the version displayed by `--version`. An empty or non-canonical value is treated as unset for package selection and updates.

  `COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS`: comma-separated list of additional directories to search for custom instructions files (in addition to git root and current working directory).

  `COPILOT_DISABLE_DESKTOP_NOTIFICATIONS`: set to "1" to suppress desktop notifications, even when the `notifications` setting is on.

  `COPILOT_DISABLE_LOGIN_SHELL_ENV`: set to "1" or "true" to stop re-reading your login-shell environment for the agent's shell commands. By default, on macOS and Linux, the CLI runs bash once as a login shell (`bash -l`, which reads /etc/profile and ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login, or ~/.profile, but not ~/.bashrc) and applies the PATH and variables it exports, so tools your profile activates (conda, nvm, Homebrew) are found.

  `COPILOT_DISABLE_RESUME_AUTO_CD`: set to "1" or "true" so that --resume does not switch to the working directory recorded for the resumed session.

  `COPILOT_EDITOR`, `VISUAL`, `EDITOR` (in order of precedence): command used to interactively edit a file (e.g., the plan).

  `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` (in order of precedence): an authentication token that takes precedence over previously stored credentials. Exception: in Codespaces, the auto-injected `GITHUB_TOKEN` (a user-to-server token) does not take precedence over a `/login` account. An explicitly exported `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, or `GH_TOKEN` still takes precedence.

  `COPILOT_HOME`: override the directory where configuration and state files are stored; defaults to `$HOME/.copilot`. See "Files and directories" in `copilot help config` for what it holds.

  `COPILOT_HOOK_ALLOW_HTTP_AUTH_HOOKS`: set to "1" to let preToolUse, preMcpToolCall, and permissionRequest HTTP hooks use plain http:// URLs; otherwise they must use https://.

  `COPILOT_HOOK_ALLOW_LOCALHOST`: set to "1" to let HTTP hooks post to localhost and other loopback addresses, which are otherwise blocked; plain http:// is then also accepted for those addresses.

  `COPILOT_INLINE_IMAGES_TMUX`: set to "0" to stop forwarding inline images through tmux. Forwarding also requires `allow-passthrough on` in tmux.

  `COPILOT_LOGIN_SHELL_ENV_TIMEOUT_MS`: time limit in milliseconds for reading the login-shell environment (see COPILOT_DISABLE_LOGIN_SHELL_ENV); defaults to 4000. Values that are not positive integers log a warning and use the default. If the capture fails or times out, the inherited environment is used.

  `COPILOT_LLM_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES`: maximum decoded/decompressed HTTP LLM response body (including streaming and error responses), or complete incoming WebSocket message, in bytes. Defaults to 134217728 (128 MiB). Larger responses fail the request without retrying; exactly the limit is accepted. Set before starting the process. Invalid or non-positive integers log a warning and use the default.

  `COPILOT_MASCOT_BLINK`: set to "0" to turn off the mascot's blink animation in the header.

  `COPILOT_MCP_TOOL_CACHE`: set to "false" to disable loading and persistence of MCP tool snapshots process-wide. Existing cache files are left untouched. To disable the cache for one server, set `disableToolCache` to `true` in that server's MCP configuration.

  `COPILOT_MODEL`: optionally set the agent model, including a model for a provider set with COPILOT_PROVIDER_* variables. Can be overridden by the --model command line option or the /model command.

  `COPILOT_MULTIPLEXER`: override which terminal multiplexer the CLI believes it is running directly inside. One of "tmux", "herdr", or "none"; unrecognized values are ignored. "none" declares that no multiplexer wraps this pane; it does not restore env-derived host-terminal identity inside a herdr pane, whose inherited `TERM_PROGRAM`/`WT_SESSION`-style markers describe the terminal that started the herdr server and stay untrusted. Detection is otherwise automatic from the environment. Set this when it guesses wrong — most often `COPILOT_MULTIPLEXER=tmux` for tmux running nested inside a herdr pane, because herdr panes inherit whatever `TMUX` the herdr server itself was started with.

  `COPILOT_NOTIFICATION_BATCH_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS`: maximum wait in seconds for batching completed background notifications while other notifying work runs. Accepts non-negative numbers, including fractions; 0 removes the intentional wait. Defaults to 60 for missing or invalid values. Online experiment assignments take precedence over this local value.

  `COPILOT_OFFLINE`: set to "true" to enable offline mode. When active, the CLI skips all network access: GitHub authentication, telemetry, web tools, GitHub MCP server, and auto-update are disabled. Requires a local model provider, either one you added in /model or one set with COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL. Refer to `copilot help providers`.

  `COPILOT_PAC_EVALUATION_TIMEOUT_MS`: time limit for evaluating an operating-system proxy auto-configuration (PAC) script, including queueing and DNS calls. Defaults to 10000 milliseconds (10 seconds). Set before starting Copilot. Accepts whole milliseconds from 1 to 4294967295; invalid values use the default. Does not change the separate PAC download or per-DNS-call limits.

  `COPILOT_PLUGIN_DIR_ONLY`: set to "true" to turn off automatic plugin discovery, so that only plugins passed with --plugin-dir are loaded.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG`: path of the custom model providers file; defaults to `$COPILOT_HOME/providers.json`.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`: API endpoint URL for a custom model provider (BYOK), for providers you can't add in /model and for scripts. When set, the CLI uses this provider instead of GitHub Copilot's model routing and ignores a saved `providers.json`, unless COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG names a providers file, which then wins. GitHub authentication is not required. For type "azure", use a host URL or a full project URL, including its `/api/projects/<project>` path.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE`: provider type when using BYOK. One of "openai" (default), "azure", "anthropic", or "google". Use "openai" for OpenAI-compatible endpoints including Ollama, vLLM, and Foundry Local. Use "google" (experimental) for Google's native Gemini Interactions API.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY`: API key for the custom provider. Optional for local providers like Ollama.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY_COMMAND`: shell command that prints a fresh API key for each provider request. Takes precedence over COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BEARER_TOKEN`: bearer token for custom provider authentication. For "openai", "azure" and "google" it takes precedence over COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY; "anthropic" sends both.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API`: API format for the custom provider. One of "completions" (default) or "responses". Use "responses" for GPT-5 series models.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TRANSPORT`: transport for the custom provider. One of "http" (default) or "websockets". "websockets" works only with `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai` and `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API=responses`, to use OpenAI Responses over WebSocket.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_AZURE_API_VERSION`: Azure API version when using type "azure". When omitted, uses the GA versionless v1 route. Set explicitly (e.g. "2024-10-21") to use the legacy versioned deployment route.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID`: well-known model ID used for agent configuration and token limits. Defaults to the --model value, else COPILOT_MODEL.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_MODEL`: model name sent to the provider API for inference. Defaults to the --model value, else COPILOT_MODEL, else COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS`: maximum prompt tokens for the BYOK model. Overrides both catalog and default values.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`: maximum output tokens for the BYOK model. Overrides both catalog and default values.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_VISION`: set to "true" if the BYOK model accepts image input. BYOK models are treated as text-only unless this is set, so images that tools return (such as an image file the agent views or a screenshot from an MCP server) are not sent to the model.

  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_HEADERS`: custom HTTP headers sent only to the BYOK provider endpoint (not to GitHub Copilot services). Newline-separated "Name: Value" pairs; a literal "\n" also separates entries in a double-quoted shell string. Useful for gateway keys, tenant IDs, or routing headers.

  `COPILOT_PROXY_KERBEROS`: set to "0", "false", "off", or "no" to turn off automatic Kerberos/Negotiate authentication with proxies that ask for it.

  `COPILOT_SKILLS_DIRS`: comma-separated list of additional directories to search for skills, used together with the `skillDirectories` setting. A leading `~` stands for your home directory.

  `COPILOT_SYSTEM_PROXY`: set to "0" or "false" to ignore the operating system's proxy configuration; requests then go direct unless a proxy is set with HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY or the `proxyUrl` setting.

  `COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`: in non-interactive prompt mode (-p, including -p --autopilot), how many seconds to wait for background agents and shell commands to finish before exiting; defaults to 600. "0" stops waiting at once; empty, negative, or non-numeric values use the default.

  `COPILOT_WEB_FETCH_ALLOW_LOCALHOST`: set to "1" to let the web_fetch tool fetch from hosts that resolve only to loopback addresses, such as localhost. When the sandbox is on, its `network.allowLocalNetwork` setting grants the same access.

  `GH_HOST`: GitHub hostname for authentication and API requests; defaults to "github.com". Set this to your GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency hostname (e.g., "mycompany.ghe.com"). Use when both GitHub CLI and Copilot CLI should target the same host.

  `COPILOT_GH_HOST`: GitHub hostname used only by Copilot CLI for authentication and API requests, overriding GH_HOST when set. Useful when GH_HOST points to a GitHub Enterprise Server instance but Copilot CLI needs to authenticate against github.com or a GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency hostname instead.

  `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` (case-insensitive): proxy server URL for outgoing HTTP and HTTPS connections respectively (e.g., "http://proxy.example.com:8080").

  `NO_COLOR`: when set (to any value), disables color output. See https://no-color.org/ for details.

  `NO_PROXY` (case-insensitive): comma-separated list of hostnames or patterns that should bypass the proxy (e.g., "localhost,127.0.0.1,.example.com").

  `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP`: when set to "false", uses the ripgrep binary from PATH instead of the bundled version.

  `USE_TGREP`: when set to "true", enables tgrep indexed search regardless of repository size, and also overrides the automatic-start checks described here (it does not override whether indexed search is available for your account, and `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=false` still disables it). tgrep starts even outside a git repository, indexing the working directory itself (so avoid forcing it somewhere large, such as a home directory or filesystem root), and even on a virtualized or network filesystem (for example a VFS for Git checkout, or an SMB or 9p mount). Forcing tgrep also bypasses the Windows cloud-sync safety check, even if detection fails; indexing cloud-sync folders can download cloud-only files. When set to "false", disables tgrep and uses ripgrep. When unset, tgrep is enabled automatically only inside a git repository whose root is neither the user's home directory nor a filesystem root, on a non-virtualized filesystem, and at or above the file-count threshold (50,000 files with the current configuration); Windows cloud-sync folders and detection failures still disable automatic tgrep startup, and ripgrep is used otherwise.

  Automatic startup skips Git roots that are the user's home directory or a filesystem root (including Windows drive and network-share roots) before counting files or reserving a server slot, even when the session starts in one of their subdirectories. If the home directory cannot be determined, automatic startup is also skipped. Separate repositories beneath these directories remain eligible, with or without a Git remote. `USE_TGREP=true` explicitly permits indexing these otherwise-excluded roots.

  Git worktrees from the same repository share one tgrep daemon, identified by their canonical Git common directory. Sessions starting at the same committed tree share an immutable base index, even on different branches, while edits, untracked files, and deletions remain private to each worktree. Managed-v2 is enabled by default for eligible repositories, with bounded retention and adaptive advancement to the worktree's own committed HEAD when overlay-cost thresholds are met. Unrelated clones never share a base. Non-Git folders and repositories without a commit retain single-root indexing.

  The built-in managed policy admits two repository daemons and two work slots per cache, with a 64 GiB aggregate storage budget, a 16 GiB allocation per repository, and an 8 GiB retention target per repository. Each daemon uses one indexing worker; staging and private-work reservations are each capped at 16 GiB in aggregate and 8 GiB per repository. These are accounting limits, not upfront allocations or hard process-memory limits. Admission and maintenance run in the background; searches scan until their view is ready. Shared bases live outside disposable worktrees under `tgrep-shared/tgrep-managed-v2`. Runtime shutdown reaps owned daemons after local session teardown; peers reconnect using authoritative pins. External servers are not killed or covered by the managed-daemon cap.

  `USE_TGREP_MANAGED`: set to "false" to opt out of managed-v2 and restore v1 fixed-pin/retain-all compatibility, including its one-server limit. This overrides `TGREP_SHARED_CONFIG` without reading that file. Unset or "true" selects managed-v2; other values are rejected. This flag does not force indexing or bypass eligibility. `USE_TGREP=false` disables all tgrep indexing and runtime cache maintenance.

  `TGREP_SHARED_CONFIG`: optional path to a complete managed-v2 JSON configuration overriding the built-in defaults. Durations are milliseconds and sizes are bytes; missing fields and invalid files are rejected, not merged with defaults. All managed processes sharing a cache must use the same effective configuration. Use `/index status`, `/index advance <commit>`, and `/index policy <version> <file>` to inspect or change authoritative state. `/index collect` only previews; `/index collect --run` authorizes collection. Before removing a worktree, require `/index release` to acknowledge `root_handles_released: true`; a busy response is not permission to delete. Scheduled tgrep-owned reclamation includes deleted repositories while an eligible Copilot host runs; no operating-system service is installed. Opting out does not convert or delete existing managed storage. See `copilot-runtime-requirements.md` in the runtime repository for configuration and rollout details.

  `TGREP_FILE_COUNT_THRESHOLD`: minimum file count for automatic tgrep indexed search. Accepts a non-negative integer, ignoring surrounding whitespace. Defaults to 10,000 on Windows and 50,000 on other platforms. Invalid values log a warning and use the platform default. Automatic sessions must meet this threshold before reusing an existing index and recheck it before taking over its server. Setting it to 0 removes only the file-count requirement; all other automatic-start checks still apply. `USE_TGREP=true` bypasses this threshold, and `USE_TGREP=false` still disables tgrep.

  `USE_TGREP_WARM_START`: when set to "true", blocks Copilot CLI startup until the tgrep index is ready when tgrep starts. It does not enable tgrep on its own; pair with `USE_TGREP=true` to force indexing and wait for readiness. Useful for evaluating tgrep search against a warm index.

  Set by Copilot CLI for processes it starts:

  `COPILOT_CLI`: "1" in the agent's shell commands and in hooks, so scripts such as git hooks can tell they run under Copilot CLI.

  `COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID`: the current session's ID, in the agent's shell commands.

  `COPILOT_PROJECT_DIR`: the repository root, or the working directory outside a repository, in hooks (also as `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`).

  `COPILOT_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `COPILOT_PLUGIN_DATA`: a plugin's installation directory and its data directory, in that plugin's hooks (also as `PLUGIN_ROOT`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`).

  `COPILOT_HOOK_DIR`: in a command hook, the directory of the file that defines it.

  `COPILOT_HOOK_DEPTH`: in a command hook, how many hook launches lead to it ("1" when the CLI was not itself started from a hook), so a hook can stop sessions that keep launching each other.

  `COPILOT_TRACEPARENT`, `COPILOT_TRACESTATE`: in a command hook, the W3C trace context of the operation that ran it, when there is one.

  `COPILOT_SESSION_CWD`: the session's working directory, for `${COPILOT_SESSION_CWD}` references in LSP and local MCP server configs.

  OpenTelemetry / Monitoring:

  `COPILOT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`: set to "true" before startup to disable Copilot-owned GitHub and Entra authentication telemetry process-wide, like `--disable-client-telemetry`. Does not affect independently configured OpenTelemetry, server-side telemetry, or OS/broker telemetry.

  `COPILOT_INSTALLATION_TELEMETRY`: set to "true" before starting the CLI or SDK runtime process to enable installation-token telemetry discovery. Defaults to off; "false" also overrides COPILOT_CLI_ENABLED_FEATURE_FLAGS. Disabled processes neither request nor use cached installation metadata. Requires server authorization and normal telemetry consent; does not change inference, user-token telemetry, or OpenTelemetry. Restart the runtime process to change it.

  `COPILOT_OTEL_ENABLED`: set to "true" to explicitly enable OpenTelemetry instrumentation.

  `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`: OTLP endpoint URL. Setting this automatically enables OTel.

| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BEARER_TOKEN` | Bearer token; for `anthropic` the CLI sends both this and the API key |
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API` | `completions` (default) or `responses` |
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TRANSPORT` | `http` (default) or `websockets` |
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_AZURE_API_VERSION` | Azure only |
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID` | "well-known model ID used for agent configuration and token limits" |
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_MODEL` | Model name sent to the provider |
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS` | Overrides catalog and default values |
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | Overrides catalog and default values |
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_VISION` | `"true"` if the model accepts images; otherwise BYOK models are text-only |
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_HEADERS` | Extra headers sent only to the BYOK endpoint |
| `COPILOT_MODEL` | The agent model |
| `COPILOT_OFFLINE` | Skips GitHub auth, telemetry, web tools and auto-update; needs a BYOK provider |

**What it confirms**
- **Vision** has a variable (`COPILOT_PROVIDER_VISION`), as you said.
- **Adaptive thinking and the supported reasoning-effort levels have no variable** in this version. The only reasoning control is the per-run `--reasoning-effort` flag. So an env-only setup can match `providers.json` on type, token limits, vision and model identity, but not on those two capability flags.
- **It explains the bug we just fixed.** The help says a `COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG` file wins over `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`. That's why setting `COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG` made the CLI ignore AWF's sidecar address and dial the gateway directly.

One caveat: the CI runner uses whatever CLI version gh-aw installs, which may differ from your 1.0.118.

The fix-branch run is still going. I'll report back when it finishes.

**Problem:** Every request fails with `503` and the Squid access log shows
`TCP_MISS/503 ... HIER_NONE`, or AWF aborts at startup with
"The awf-net subnet 172.30.0.0/24 contains the DNS resolver(s) ...".

**Cause:** The default `awf-net` subnet (`172.30.0.0/24`) overlaps the host or
cluster network. On OpenShift/ARO it is inside the default service CIDR
(`172.30.0.0/16`) and the CoreDNS ClusterIP is exactly `172.30.0.10` — the
address AWF assigns to Squid, so Squid sends its DNS queries to itself.

**Solution:** Relocate the network to a free RFC1918 block:

```bash
sudo awf --network-subnet 10.88.0.0/24 --allow-domains github.com -- curl https://github.com
```

Or in an AWF config file:

```json
{ "network": { "subnet": "10.88.0.0/24" } }
```

cluster network. On OpenShift/ARO it is inside the default service CIDR
(`172.30.0.0/16`) and the CoreDNS ClusterIP is exactly `172.30.0.10` — the
address AWF assigns to Squid, so Squid sends its DNS queries to itself.

**Solution:** Relocate the network to a free RFC1918 block:

```bash
sudo awf --network-subnet 10.88.0.0/24 --allow-domains github.com -- curl https://github.com
```

Or in an AWF config file:

```json
{ "network": { "subnet": "10.88.0.0/24" } }
```

# model-catalog: false passes the model through verbatim. Neither gateway serves
# /models, so gh-aw's default pre-run catalogue lookup would stop the run with
# catalog_unavailable. Needs gh-aw v1.4.0 or later.
engine:
  id: copilot
  model: lab-proxy/claude-opus-5-5
  model-catalog: false
  env:
    COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL: https://anthropic-oauth-proxy.tailfb3ea.ts.net
    COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY: unused-gateway-strips-auth
    COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG: ${{ github.workspace }}/.github/aw/providers.json
# Both gateways are reachable only on the tailnet, so every job that calls the
# model joins it first: the agent and the threat-detection job.
jobs:
  agent:
    setup-steps:
      - name: Connect to tailnet
        uses: tailscale/github-action@064b10558093f38325e838ddea35486bdc6b1d5c # v4.4.0
        with:
          oauth-client-id: ${{ secrets.TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          audience: ${{ secrets.TS_AUDIENCE }}
          tags: tag:ci
  detection:
    setup-steps:
      - name: Connect to tailnet
        uses: tailscale/github-action@064b10558093f38325e838ddea35486bdc6b1d5c # v4.4.0
        with:
          oauth-client-id: ${{ secrets.TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          audience: ${{ secrets.TS_AUDIENCE }}
          tags: tag:ci
strict: true
network:
  # The primary gateway host is added automatically from
  # COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL; the fallback gateway must be listed here.
  allowed: [defaults, github, agents.tailfb3ea.ts.net]
tools:
  github:
    mode: gh-proxy
    toolsets: [default, actions]
  cache-memory:

content.text:
The sidecar fix worked, but the run hit the next problem: DNS. I've pushed a fix for that too, and a new run has started from the fix branch: [run 46143362287](https://github.com/basher83/tailnet-microservices/actions/runs/46143362287). I'm watching it in the background.

**What the last run showed** ([46142756888](https://github.com/basher83/tailnet-microservices/actions/runs/46142756888))
- **Model name:** the CLI now sends requests to the sidecar (`api-proxy:10002`). gh-aw used the model name as given: `engine.model-catalog is false; using 'lab-proxy/claude-opus-5-5' verbatim`.
- **New failure:** every request came back `503`. The run's firewall logs explain why:
  - Squid, the sandbox's outbound proxy, logged `CONNECT 503 TCP_TUNNEL:HIER_NONE anthropic-oauth-proxy.tailfb3ea.ts.net:443`.
  - The sidecar recorded the response header `x-squid-error: ERR_DNS_FAIL 0`.
  - Squid's config had `dns_nameservers 168.63.129.16`. That's Azure's resolver, which AWF reads from the runner's `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf` and which knows nothing about `*.ts.net`.

**The fix** (commit `952313b`)
- **Rejected route:** AWF's `--dns-servers` flag would have been the direct fix, but gh-aw's strict mode rejects passing flags to AWF (`sandbox.agent.args`) as "an internal implementation detail". Turning strict off would loosen every safety check to pass one flag.
- **What I did instead:** added a setup step in the agent and detection jobs, right after the Tailscale step. It runs `resolvectl` to put MagicDNS (`100.100.100.100`) first on the runner's default network interface, with Azure's resolver kept second. AWF reads that resolver list when it starts, so Squid gets both servers.
- **Early check:** the step fails right away with a clear error if MagicDNS can't resolve the gateway. It only warns if MagicDNS can't resolve a public name (`api.github.com`). In that case Squid should fall back to Azure, but I'm not sure it does when MagicDNS returns an error rather than timing out.

**Not yet tested:**
- Whether Squid's container can reach `100.100.100.100` through the runner's Tailscale interface.
- Whether MagicDNS still answers public names on a CI node.

The new step logs its result either way.

content.text:
The network path now works end to end, and the model answered through your gateway. What stops the run now is gh-aw's own model check, and it can't be fixed while we use `providers.json`.

**What run [46143362287](https://github.com/basher83/tailnet-microservices/actions/runs/46143362287) showed**
- **DNS fix worked:** AWF picked up `nameserver 100.100.100.100` first, and Squid logged `CONNECT 200 TCP_TUNNEL:HIER_DIRECT anthropic-oauth-proxy.tailfb3ea.ts.net:443`.
- **The model ran:** it answered and made its first tool call, reading the run window (25 runs, 21 failures).
- **The block:** about 7 seconds in, gh-aw's runtime guard killed the CLI:
  > Model 'lab-proxy/claude-opus-5-5' is not available as configured: Copilot substituted 'claude-opus-5-5'. Refusing silent model substitution.
- **Harmless noise:** the `/models` 400s from your proxy come from gh-aw's model-list probe, which sends a GET with an empty body. The probe isn't used since the model catalog is off.

**Why it's a dead end with `providers.json`**
- **The guard:** it compares the configured name against the model the CLI reports. The only prefix gh-aw strips is `copilot/` or `github-copilot/` (`normalizeForCopilotCLI` in v1.4.1). gh-aw's SDK driver does reconcile `providers.json` prefixes, but the SDK driver requires the model catalog, which we had to turn off.
- **The CLI:** I tested your local CLI (1.0.118) against dummy servers that record each request:

| Setup | Request sent? |
|---|---|
| `providers.json`, `--model lab-proxy/claude-opus-5-5` | Yes, to `lab-proxy`, with `model=claude-opus-5-5` (the name the guard sees) |
| `providers.json`, bare `--model claude-opus-5-5` (shared or unique id) | No: `Model "claude-opus-5-5" is not available` |
| No `providers.json`, environment variables only, bare `claude-opus-5-5` | Yes, to `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, with `model=claude-opus-5-5` |

So a `providers.json` model has to be named `provider/model`, and gh-aw's guard rejects that form every time.

**Proposed fix: environment variables only**
- **Delete:** `.github/aw/providers.json` and `COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG`.
- **Set:** `model: claude-opus-5-5` (bare), plus `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE: anthropic`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID: claude-opus-5-5`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_VISION: "true"`, and the two token-limit variables.
- **What it fixes:** inside the sandbox, AWF already points `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` at its sidecar, so the hard-coded `172.30.0.30:10002` goes away too. This is the setup the AWF docs describe.
- **What you lose:**
  - **Two capability settings:** `adaptive_thinking: "required"` and the `reasoning_effort` list have no variables. The CLI uses its built-in defaults for `claude-opus-5-5` instead. A specific effort level can still be set per run with `?effort=high`.
  - **Aperture as a second option:** to use it, you'd change `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` to Aperture's address instead.

I haven't checked which model name the CLI writes to its session events in this setup; my test server returned errors, so no reply was logged. The request itself carried bare `claude-opus-5-5`, which matches what the guard would expect.

**Separately:** gh-aw's CLI-mode check not handling `providers.json` prefixes, when its SDK-mode check does, looks like an upstream gap worth filing on github/gh-aw. I haven't filed anything.

Everything is on `claude/ci-triage-sidecar-endpoint`; `main` hasn't changed since the merge. Should I switch to environment variables only and drop `providers.json`, or keep `providers.json`?

# Tailscale's workload-identity login (oauth-client-id + audience) mints a
  # GitHub OIDC token. Same pattern as openwiki-update.yml.
  id-token: write
# BYOK: inference goes to gateways on the tailnet, not GitHub Copilot.
# .github/aw/providers.json is what the Copilot CLI uses: both providers, the
# model capabilities, and the wire type. Models are selected as
# <provider>/<model-id>:
#   lab-proxy          -> AWF API-proxy sidecar -> anthropic-oauth-proxy, in use
#   aperture-anthropic -> Aperture on agents.tailfb3ea.ts.net; switch `model:`
#                         to aperture-anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 to use it
#
# Request path for lab-proxy: the agent never dials the gateway itself. AWF
# keeps the real upstream in its API-proxy sidecar, and inside the sandbox the
# Copilot listener is http://172.30.0.30:10002 (what AWF sets
# COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL to there). providers.json overrides that variable,
# so lab-proxy's baseUrl must be the sidecar address itself; pointing it at the
# gateway's https URL bypasses the sidecar and fails with a TLS "wrong version
# number" error (run 46142203840).
#
# COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL (outside the sandbox) is the sidecar's upstream: the
# real gateway. It also makes gh-aw compile the run as BYOK (no
# COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN check) and allowlists the gateway host.
# COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY is a placeholder: the sidecar refuses keyless
# upstreams (503), and the gateway strips client auth headers in OAuth mode, so
# the value never matters. Avoid a bare "-": gh-aw emits it unquoted and the
# generated YAML breaks. COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE is not needed: providers.json
# sets the type.
#
# No fallback-models: gh-aw's fallback retries the same provider with another
# model name, and cross-provider chains are not supported
# (https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/engines/#ordered-model-fallback-fallback-models).
#
# model-catalog: false passes the model through verbatim. Neither gateway serves
# /models, so gh-aw's default pre-run catalogue lookup would stop the run with
# catalog_unavailable. Needs gh-aw v1.4.0 or later.
engine:
  id: copilot
  model: lab-proxy/claude-opus-5-5
  model-catalog: false
  env:
    COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL: https://anthropic-oauth-proxy.tailfb3ea.ts.net
    COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY: unused-gateway-strips-auth
    COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG: ${{ github.workspace }}/.github/aw/providers.json
# Both gateways are reachable only on the tailnet, so every job that calls the
# model joins it first: the agent and the threat-detection job.
#
# DNS: the AWF egress proxy (Squid) resolves every outbound host itself, using
# the servers AWF reads from /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf when it starts.
# On the runner that file lists only Azure's resolver, so *.ts.net names failed
# with ERR_DNS_FAIL (run 46142756888). The second setup step puts MagicDNS
# (100.100.100.100) first on the default interface, ahead of Azure's resolver,
# and fails early if MagicDNS can't resolve the gateway. AWF's --dns-servers
# flag would do the same, but strict mode rejects sandbox.agent.args.
jobs:
  agent:
    setup-steps:
      - name: Connect to tailnet
        uses: tailscale/github-action@064b10558093f38325e838ddea35486bdc6b1d5c # v4.4.0
        with:
          oauth-client-id: ${{ secrets.TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          audience: ${{ secrets.TS_AUDIENCE }}
          tags: tag:ci
      - name: Put MagicDNS first for the AWF egress proxy
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          iface="$(ip route show default | awk '{print $5; exit}')"
          upstream="$(resolvectl dns "$iface" | sed 's/^[^:]*://')"
          sudo resolvectl dns "$iface" 100.100.100.100 $upstream
          echo "AWF will read:"; grep '^nameserver' /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf
          dig +short @100.100.100.100 anthropic-oauth-proxy.tailfb3ea.ts.net | grep -q . \
            || { echo "::error::MagicDNS did not resolve anthropic-oauth-proxy.tailfb3ea.ts.net"; exit 1; }
          dig +short @100.100.100.100 api.github.com | grep -q . \
            || echo "::warning::MagicDNS did not resolve a public name; Squid will fall back to $upstream"
  detection:
    setup-steps:
      - name: Connect to tailnet
        uses: tailscale/github-action@064b10558093f38325e838ddea35486bdc6b1d5c # v4.4.0
        with:
          oauth-client-id: ${{ secrets.TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          audience: ${{ secrets.TS_AUDIENCE }}

copilot/ prefix. The two can't both be satisfied.

  Adaptive thinking and the reasoning-effort list have no variables and
  come from the CLI's defaults for the model id.
- AWF now rewrites COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL to its sidecar inside the
  sandbox, so the hard-coded sidecar address is gone.
- Drop Aperture's host from network.allowed; switching to Aperture is now
  a COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL change, which allowlists its host.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
I switched the workflow to environment variables only, and a test run has started: [run 46144142336](https://github.com/basher83/tailnet-microservices/actions/runs/46144142336). It's using the fix branch `claude/ci-triage-sidecar-endpoint` (commit `da14502`), and I'm watching it in the background.

**What changed**
- **Removed:** `.github/aw/providers.json` and `COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG`. That also gets rid of the hard-coded sidecar address: inside the sandbox, AWF now points `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` at its sidecar on its own.
- **Model:** `claude-opus-5-5`, with no `lab-proxy/` prefix, so it should pass gh-aw's model check.
- **Settings, all in `engine.env`:**

  | Variable | Value |
  |---|---|
  | `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` | `https://anthropic-oauth-proxy.tailfb3ea.ts.net` (the address the sidecar forwards to) |
  | `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE` | `anthropic` |
  | `COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY` | placeholder; the sidecar requires a key, and your gateway strips it |
  | `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID` | `claude-opus-5-5` |
  | `COPILOT_PROVIDER_VISION` | `true` |
  | `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS` / `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | `872000` / `128000` |

- **Aperture:** its host is off the firewall allowlist. Switching to Aperture is now a one-line change to `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, which allowlists its host automatically.
- **Kept:** the Tailscale and MagicDNS setup steps, the OpenAI evals judge, and the schedules.
- **Workflow comment:** rewritten to explain why there's no `providers.json` and where adaptive thinking and reasoning effort now come from.

The lock compiled strict with 0 warnings. It has all seven variables, no `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` check, and the gateway on the allowlist.

**Open:** which model name the CLI writes to its session events with this setup. My local test sent bare `claude-opus-5-5` on the wire, so I expect it to pass gh-aw's model check, but this run is the real test.
